story.iWant: MCP document ingestion to complete without timing out
story.soThat: users can ingest financial PDFs via the MCP interface without errors
story.tasks: - Task 1: Investigate current MCP ingestion timeout (measure times, identify bottlenecks, check config) - Task 2: Optimize ingestion performance (enable pypdfium, parallelism, batch embeddings) - Task 3: Implement async ingestion for large documents (REQUIRED for 150-200 page PDFs) - Task 4: Create end-to-end validation test (sync and async ingestion paths) - Task 5: Update MCP documentation (timeout config, ingestion times, troubleshooting)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC1: PDF ingestion completes within MCP timeout (60-120s) for typical documents (up to ~50 pages). Large PDFs (150-200 pages) handled via async ingestion (AC5). AC2: Optimize ingestion performance using pypdfium backend (Story 2.1) and page-level parallelism (Story 2.2). Target: <60s for 20-30 pages. AC3: Integration test validates MCP ingestion → query flow without timeout. AC4: MCP timeout configuration documented with expected ingestion times table. AC5: Async ingestion for large documents (150-200 pages) - REQUIRED. Support both sync (small docs) and async (large docs) ingestion modes.

doc.title: Epic 3 Retrospective
doc.section: ACTION ITEM 3: Investigate & Fix MCP Ingestion Timeout
doc.snippet: MCP ingestion tool times out during document processing. Root cause: Large PDF ingestion (Docling + embedding generation) exceeds 60-120s MCP timeout. 160-page PDF takes 3-5+ minutes. Fix options: optimize performance, async ingestion pattern.

doc.title: Story 4.0.5 - Test vs Production Database Separation
doc.snippet: Small test fixture available: tests/fixtures/sample-small-3-pages.pdf (4 pages, 228 KB). Integration tests configured to use small fixture by default (15-18x speedup). Environment-based configuration pattern established via Settings.app_env.

doc.title: Epic 2 - Advanced RAG Architecture Enhancement
doc.snippet: pypdfium backend provides 1.7-2.5x speedup and 50-60% memory reduction for Docling PDF processing. Story 2.2 implements page-level parallelism for concurrent page processing.

doc.title: Technology Stack
doc.snippet: Docling with pypdfium backend (97.9% table accuracy, 1.7-2.5x speedup). FastMCP (MCP Python SDK) exposes tools via MCP protocol. Fin-E5 embeddings for semantic vectors.

doc.title: Complete Reference Implementation
doc.snippet: FastMCP tool pattern: @mcp.tool() decorator, Pydantic models for request/response, structured logging with extra={}, async/await for I/O operations.

dependencies.python: fastmcp: "Latest" (MCP Python SDK) docling: "Latest" (PDF processing with pypdfium backend) qdrant-client: "1.11+" (Vector storage) pydantic: "2.x" (Data validation and settings) pytest: "Latest" (Testing framework) pytest-asyncio: "Latest" (Async test support)

story-context.constraints: - MCP has default timeout limits (60-120 seconds for synchronous operations) - Large PDFs (150-200 pages) are typical production use case - MUST be supported - Cannot increase timeout beyond ~120s without poor UX (user waiting too long) - Must maintain 97.9% table accuracy from Docling (no quality regression) - Async ingestion requires job tracking (in-memory OK for MVP, no persistence needed) - Test environment uses small fixtures (sample-small-3-pages.pdf) for fast validation - Production database separation established (Story 4.0.5) - tests use port 6335/5433 - All I/O operations must be async/await - Use structured logging with extra={} for context - Type hints and Google-style docstrings required

tests.standards: Use pytest with pytest-asyncio for async tests. Test fixtures in tests/fixtures/. Use small fixture (sample-small-3-pages.pdf) for fast unit/integration tests. Test environment auto-configured via conftest.py (APP_ENV=test, ports 6335/5433). Integration tests validate end-to-end MCP → ingestion → query flow. Measure and validate performance improvements (baseline vs optimized). Test both sync and async ingestion paths. Type hints and structured logging required.
tests.locations: tests/unit/ - Unit tests for ingestion pipeline components tests/integration/ - End-to-end MCP ingestion tests tests/fixtures/ - Test fixtures (sample-small-3-pages.pdf)
tests.ideas: AC1: Test sync ingestion completes within timeout (10-page: <30s, 30-page: <90s) AC2: Test pypdfium backend enabled, page-level parallelism working AC3: Integration test: ingest 10-page PDF via MCP, verify chunks stored, query returns results AC3: Integration test: async ingestion with 150-page PDF (verify status polling, eventual completion) AC4: Validate MCP timeout configuration documented AC5: Test async job tracking (create job, poll status, retrieve result) Performance: Measure baseline vs optimized ingestion times (assert improvement) Error handling: Test timeout scenarios, file not found, invalid PDF
